Posted October 23, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: This article is an excellent example of how even safe driving education is subordinated to the ideological requirements of marijuana prohibition.)
October 23, 2000
From The Herald Sun
hseditor@hwt.newsltd.com.au
http://www.heraldsun.com.au/
By Peter Mickelburough And Mark Buttler
(MarijuanaNews note: The Herald Sun is a tabloid owned by Rupert Murdock. That may excuse the breathless style, but not the factless reporting.)

DRUGGED DRIVING ON THE RISE

THE shocking extent of the growing drug menace on our roads is revealed in a national survey of drivers. An alarming one in nine motorists admitted driving under the influence of recreational drugs such as marijuana and cocaine.
(MarijuanaNews note: This typical lumping marijuana with cocaine sends the message, " Yes, kiddies, marijuana is the same as cocaine, so you can use cocaine as safely as marijuana. " )

The deadly practice was worst among young drivers, with more than one in four 18 to 34-year-old males saying they had driven after taking recreational drugs.

In the annual AAMI crash index survey, one in four motorists admitted ignoring warnings against driving after taking medicines.
See
They Are Legal, So They Must Be Safe: " Teens Abusing Drugstore Medicines "
Should We Have Drug-Free Drugstores?
Context For Medical Marijuana and " Drug Education " Debates
and
Oregon Wants To Ban Driving While Using Over-The-Counter Drugs

Police said drug-driving was a growing problem that would be fought with new laws allowing drivers to be tested for drug impairment for the first time from December.
See
Road Toll Lowest In 2 Decades
So Australian State of Queensland to Begin Road Tests For Drivers On " Drugs " ???

" It's increasing and that's obviously a concern, and that's probably reflected in general drug use in the community, " said Supt Bob Wylie, of the traffic support division.

The AAMI survey also found:

ALMOST unanimous support for random driver drug tests.
See
Random Drug Testing At Work Drives Employees To Swap Cannabis For Hard Drugs --
UK Report

SPEEDING was still acceptable to almost half of drivers.

A SHARP fall in those who thought speedsters did not get caught.

WIDESPREAD concern about the risks posed by older drivers.

A DROP in road rage tendencies.

The survey showed the most reckless drivers were young males, NSW and ACT drivers, the inexperienced, and those who had been prosecuted for drink-driving, had received several speeding fines or had been in an accident.

AAMI corporate affairs director Richard Jeffery said it was disturbing that one in 12 drivers believed drug-driving was safer than drink-driving.
See
UK Study Finds Marijuana Use Makes Drivers Safer. Now The Prohibitionists Can’t Hide the Study, So They Will Just Ignore It.
(MarijuanaNews note: The author of this study said, " If you were to ask me to rank them in order of priority, fatigue is the worst killer, followed by alcohol, and drugs follow way behind in third. "

Mr Jeffery said it also was disturbing some people believed recreational drug use did not make people aggressive drivers.
(MarijuanaNews note: U.S. Department of Transportation study on marijuana and driving shows THC appears to affect drivers in dramatically different ways than alcohol --

" After alcohol, there was a tendency towards faster driving, and after THC, slower… Our city driving study showed that drivers who drank alcohol over-estimated their performance quality, whereas those who smoked marijuana under-estimated it. This evidence suggests that alcohol encourages risky driving, whereas THC encourages greater caution. " )

From
A Remarkable Article Comparing The Effects of Marijuana and Alcohol On Driving

" After all these years of education and the worldwide evidence of the disastrous effects drugs can have, it is extraordinary that these people still have these attitudes and behaviors, " he said.
(MarijuanaNews note: He is concerned that people believe something that is supported by an overwhelming amount of data.)

Consulting psychologist John Cheetham called for education at venues where drugs were used -- nightclubs, dance parties and raves.

Mr Cheetham said signs should be posted at such venues warning of the dangers of drug-driving.

" We should introduce an awareness of the effects of recreational drug use and fatigue on driving into pre-licence testing, " he said.

Drug-driving claims about 50 lives a year in Victoria with associated costs of more than $143 million.

Victorian Institute of Forensic Medicine research on fatal accidents shows drugs are found more often than alcohol in a deceased driver's blood samples.
(MarijuanaNews note: " Drugs "?? What drugs are these? Lumping all " drugs " together obscures the nature of the problem.)

In 1997-98 drugs other than alcohol were involved in 32 per cent of fatalities compared with 26 per cent where alcohol was involved.

The Institute's Dr Olaf Drummer said amphetamines were found in a quarter of all fatally injured truck drivers.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is not " recreational use " but a part of the problem of fatigue.)

While 5 per cent of 35 to 54-year-old males admitted driving under the influence of speed, its use was higher among 18 to 34-year-old males where one in 11 also admitted using the stimulant.

From December 1, new laws will allow police to video suspect drivers as they complete a series of eye and balance tests. Those who fail will be forced to give blood and urine samples for drug testing. Those who test positive face jail, fines up to $2500 and loss of licence for up to four years.

Supt Wylie said the new tests would allow police to check drug impairment and for the first time give some indication of the true size of the drug driving problem.

Of the 770 drivers surveyed, one in 10 supported random police drug-driving tests. One in 10 also said nobody should drive after recreational drug use and they would try to stop a person they knew driving if he/she had been using drugs.
(MarijuanaNews note: The effect of almost all drugs is dose related. People can safely drive after having a small amount of alcohol and many other drugs.)
See
Australian Judge Says: " I do not find you were so affected by cannabis as to lose control. "

One in 12 of respondents believed driving after taking drugs was safer than drink-driving and one in 20 did not believe a small amount of recreational drug use was a safety risk while driving.
(MarijuanaNews note: Which is supported by the data.)
See
Canadian Study Confirms That Marijuana Impairs Driving Far Less Than Alcohol
and
1994 Dutch Study On " Marijuana Use And Driving " In Real World Conditions

One in 25 said it would not affect their driving.

A police source said there seemed to be a widespread notion that driving while " stoned " was not dangerous.

But Dr Drummer said institute research indicated that people who were affected by marijuana were five times more likely to be the cause of a fatal accident.
(MarijuanaNews note: More likely than what? Such a finding is not consistent with any of the large scale studies that I have seen published. In fact, it is contradicted by the largest such study which – as it happens -- was done in Australia. See
Australian Study Of 2,500 Injured Drivers Showed Those Who Used Marijuana
Less Likely To Have Caused Accident Than Even Drug-Free Drivers
– But How Do The Swedish Prohibitionists Report It?

In any case, we will now see this " fact " accepted in the prohibitionist propaganda, just like the NIDA monkeys and the " potent pot traded for cocaine " stories.

Would it be too much to expect of the reporters to ask them to provide the source of this " data? " Probably.)


The widely held belief that young drivers -- especially males -- were the most dangerous was supported by the AAMI survey results.
(MarijuanaNews note: Stop the presses! That is one of the best documented facts. Young males are the most aggressive members of society. Young males have the highest rate of use of alcohol and other drugs, including marijuana. They are also the most likely to commit most types of crime, etc. These facts greatly complicate any study of the impact of alcohol and other drugs on social problems, including most accidents, as noted below. For example, there is probably a correlation between most social problems and wearing sneakers, which are worn by most young men. Does wearing sneakers cause these problems?)

Young male drivers aged 18-24 topped the list for having the most aggressive attitudes, being most likely to drink-drive, speed, be reckless behind the wheel, have bad driver habits and be involved in a crash.

Other high-risk groups were blue-collar workers, those with less than 10 years' driving experience and those who had been caught drink-driving, received multiple speeding fines or been involved in an accident.
(MarijuanaNews note: Surprise, surprise!)

The survey also found that drivers aged over 55, particularly women, had the safest attitudes to driving, although elderly drivers are increasingly being seen as road hazards.
